title: Design System: any-to-bench
scope: site/ — the landing page (src/App.svelte), the bundle viewer (src/Viewer.svelte), and src/lib/. The Python CLI and docs/ are out of scope.

stock.usage: Every surface a word is read on. DaisyUI base-100.

stock-shaded.usage: Second-order panel ground on the card. DaisyUI base-200.

bed.usage: The page ground under every card. Content is never set on it except the footer's issuing block.

bed-deep.usage: Scrollbar track — the shadowed part of the bed.

bed-content.usage: The only text color permitted directly on the bed.

graphite.usage: Content that counts: headlines, question numbers, exam prose, the filled mark, 2px boundary rules. DaisyUI base-content.

graphite-soft.usage: Supporting prose, captions, point values, secondary labels.

dropout.usage: The ink the scanner is blind to: the measuring grid, dividing rules, footer links, separators. Never carries anything a grader depends on.

dropout-ink.usage: Drop-out cyan where it must still be read: field captions, register stub numbers, the unfilled mark's outline.

dropout-soft.usage: Every cell seam, table row rule, and panel border on stock. DaisyUI base-300.

dropout-faint.usage: The ground of an opened answer key, a hovered register stub, and the travelling band in the question rail.

cinnabar.usage: Fills only: the act that commits, the broken seal's hover, the error glyph, the focus outline, the caret.

cinnabar-ink.usage: Cinnabar as text or hairline: the sealed-key label and border, matching-rule answer arrows.

cinnabar-deep.usage: The hover darkening under white text on the primary action. Written literally at both call sites; promote to a :root custom property before a third use.

display.purpose: One per page, on the issued card. Set to a 19ch measure with text-balance so it breaks like a printed heading.

headline.purpose: Section heads. The viewer's first-run heading is the same voice at clamp(2.1rem, 5vw, 3.6rem) / 800.

title.purpose: In-panel headings. Exam section titles take the same rank at 1.25rem in the Han face.

body.purpose: Prose at a 62–68ch measure. The landing lede steps up to 1.125rem; in-panel copy steps down to 0.9375rem.

label.purpose: The .field-label — uppercase, letterspaced, set in drop-out ink so it disappears under the scanner lamp. Names a value; never a kicker or eyebrow.

mono.purpose: Question numbers, stub numbers, points, bundle names, dataset ids, commands, JSON. Ranges 0.6875rem to 1.875rem; question numbers are the loud end at semibold graphite.

han.purpose: Traditional Chinese exam content. TC face leads, line-height 1.9, overflow-wrap: anywhere — bundles are untrusted input and must not set the page width.

shadows.name: sheet
shadows.value: 0 1px 0 color-mix(in oklab, #fff 55%, transparent) inset, 0 18px 44px -18px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.72), 0 2px 6px -2px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.45)
shadows.purpose: The only shadow in the system: card stock lifted off the scanner bed. Inset hairline is the lit top edge; the two offset shadows are the cast shadow. Applied by .sheet and nowhere else.

motion.name: mark-fill
motion.purpose: The one authored moment: graphite growing into a square (scale 0.15 → 1) when a mark fills.

motion.name: state-color
motion.purpose: Color, background, and border transitions on rows and stubs. Nothing else animates.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Global, applied to *, ::before and ::after. No component may opt out.

buildGuards.script: site/check-css.mjs, run by pnpm build after vite build
buildGuards.why: Tailwind emits utility rules only where its scanner sees the name used, and it has dropped this world's classes twice — once because an unanchored lib/ rule in .gitignore hid site/src/lib from source detection. The world's furniture is therefore plain global CSS, Mark owns its own geometry, and the build greps the output CSS so the failure is loud.

components.name: The Sheet
components.description: The card itself, and the only container in the system: stock on the bed, zero radius, the one shadow, registration marks at the true corners and a timing track down the left edge.

Form

components.css: .ds-sheet { position: relative; background: var(--omr-stock, #f4f7f8); color: var(--omr-graphite, #1b2126); border-radius: 0; padding: 2rem 1.5rem 2rem 2.25rem; font-family: 'Archivo Variable', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; box-shadow: 0 1px 0 color-mix(in oklab, #fff 55%, transparent) inset, 0 18px 44px -18px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.72), 0 2px 6px -2px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.45); } .ds-sheet-marks { position: absolute; inset: 0; pointer-events: none; background-image: linear-gradient(var(--omr-graphite, #1b2126) 0 0), linear-gradient(var(--omr-graphite, #1b2126) 0 0), linear-gradient(var(--omr-graphite, #1b2126) 0 0), linear-gradient(var(--omr-graphite, #1b2126) 0 0); background-repeat: no-repeat; background-size: 14px 3px, 3px 14px, 14px 3px, 3px 14px; background-position: left 14px top 14px, left 14px top 14px, right 14px bottom 14px, right 14px bottom 14px; } .ds-sheet-track { position: absolute; top: 2.5rem; bottom: 2.5rem; left: 7px; width: 3px; opacity: 0.7; background-image: repeating-linear-gradient(to bottom, var(--omr-graphite, #1b2126) 0 6px, transparent 6px 14px); } .ds-sheet .ds-field-label { display: block; font-size: 0.6875rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.14em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--omr-dropout-ink, #2e7a92); } .ds-sheet-body { margin: 0.25rem 0 0; font-family: 'Spline Sans Mono Variable', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.875rem; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }

components.name: The Mark
components.description: The atom of the world: a wide square outlined in the pre-printed drop-out ink, filled with graphite when it counts. The only authored motion in the system.
components.html: filled grades by script
components.css: .ds-mark-row { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; font-family: 'Archivo Variable', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-mark { position: relative; display: inline-block; flex: none; width: 1.75rem; height: 1.25rem; border-radius: 0; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1.5px var(--omr-dropout-ink, #2e7a92); transition: box-shadow 220ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-mark::after { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: 2px; background: var(--omr-graphite, #1b2126); transform: scale(0.15); opacity: 0; transition: transform 320ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), opacity 200ms ease-out; } .ds-mark[data-filled='true']::after, .ds-mark-row:hover .ds-mark::after { transform: scale(1); opacity: 1; } .ds-mark-label { font-size: 0.8125rem; letter-spacing: 0.01em; color: var(--omr-graphite-soft, #4a555d); }

components.name: Commit Button

components.name: Seal Button
components.description: The control over an answer key, and the only three-state control in the system: sealed (outlined cinnabar ink), hovered (cinnabar fill), broken (graphite fill).

components.name: Scanner Toggle
components.description: Turns the drop-out ink off across the whole document. Off: a graphite label in a faint graphite hairline. On: a solid graphite fill.

components.name: Repo Field
components.description: A mono field on a white well, joined to a graphite submit button by a shared border. Focus turns the field's border cinnabar; the submit fill flips to cinnabar because submitting is a commit.

components.name: Register Stub
components.description: One issued bundle in the register: a drop-out ordinal, then the bundle name in mono, on stock, ruled right and bottom so the grid reads as printed paper.

components.name: Question Rail Row
components.description: The sticky way through a paper: mono question number on the left, mark on the right. The active row takes a graphite left hairline and the printed tint — never cinnabar, which is spoken for.

narrative.overview:
The surface is a Taiwanese OMR answer card lying on a scanner bed. Everything a candidate is given — the grid, the rules, the field captions, the option letters — is pre-printed in a cyan the scanner's lamp does not return, so it exists only for the human. Everything that counts is graphite: the filled square, the question number, the words of the paper itself. The product does the same thing to an exam, and the interface argues by being the thing it describes. A visitor can prove the claim in one click: scanner view is a real document state that zeroes the drop-out ink and leaves the marks standing alone.

Density is high and unapologetically clerical. Content sits on cool card stock lifted off a near-black bed by the single shadow in the whole system; the stock never rounds, never gains a second shadow, and never floats over a gradient. Type is Archivo for everything Latin and structural, Spline Sans Mono for every number that identifies something, and a Traditional Chinese face leading the stack wherever real exam prose appears — the papers are in Chinese, and the design treats that as the primary reading case rather than an i18n afterthought. Numerals are tabular everywhere, because columns of them are the point.

This world refuses three things by name: the dev-tool dark hero (the dark is a scanner bed, and content never sits on it), exam-paper pastiche (no fake staples, coffee rings, torn edges, or handwriting fonts), and stock DaisyUI (radii, depth, and noise are all zeroed in a custom `omr` theme so the component library cannot speak in its own accent).
keyCharacteristics: Zero radii throughout — card stock is guillotined, not rounded.
Exactly one elevation in the system: stock lifting off the bed.
Two-tier inks: a fill tier and a contrast-checked reading tier for both cyan and cinnabar.
Cinnabar is rationed to commitment, the seal over an answer key, and refusal.
Hairline seams (1px) instead of margins wherever cells meet.
Tabular numerals globally; mono for every identifying number.
One authored motion moment: graphite growing into a square.

rules.name: The Drop-Out Rule
rules.body: Anything pre-printed — grids, rules, field captions, option letters, stub numbers, ordinal markers — is drawn in a drop-out token and carries .drops-out when it is an element rather than a border. Anything a score depends on is graphite. If you cannot say which side a new element is on, it does not belong on the card.

rules.name: The Two-Ink Rule
rules.body: Every accent has a fill tier and a reading tier, and they are not interchangeable. Cyan fills with dropout, reads with dropout-ink. Cinnabar fills with cinnabar, reads with cinnabar-ink. Text and hairlines take the reading tier; areas take the fill tier. Never set body-sized text in a fill-tier ink.

rules.name: The Reserved Cinnabar Rule
rules.body: Cinnabar is spent on three things only: the act that commits (the primary action), the seal over an answer key, and refusal (focus rings, carets, error marks). It is never used for emphasis, decoration, hover warmth, or active navigation — the viewer's travelling band is graphite plus the printed tint for exactly this reason.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums is set on body and is never overridden. Any number that identifies a thing — question, stub, score, count — is set in the mono face; any number inside a sentence stays in Archivo.

rules.name: The Han Lead Rule
rules.body: Third-party exam content is wrapped in .han: the TC face leads, line-height opens to 1.9, and overflow-wrap: anywhere is mandatory. A bundle is untrusted input, and one unbroken token must never set the width of the page.

rules.name: The Field Caption Rule
rules.body: Uppercase letterspaced type exists in exactly one role: a printed field caption naming the value directly beneath or beside it. It is never used as a kicker above a headline, as a section eyebrow, or as button text on a primary action.

rules.name: The Hairline Seam Rule
rules.body: Where cells meet, the border belongs to the container and the gap is 1px of dropout-soft showing through. A section that ends mid-row still closes with a rule across its full width, the way a printed register does.

rules.name: The One Elevation Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one shadow in this world and it means "this is the card". Hover does not lift, modals do not float higher, and nothing gains a second shadow to signal importance. State is signalled by ink and rule, never by altitude.

rules.name: The No Halo Rule
rules.body: The sheet shadow is offset and blurred, in that order. A zero-offset glow around a surface is a screen effect; stock on a bed casts its shadow downward.

rules.name: The Zero Radius Rule
rules.body: Nothing rounds. If a control looks like it needs a radius to feel finished, it needs different padding or a different rule weight instead.

dos: Do keep the world's furniture (.sheet, .registered, .registered-marks, .timing-track, .ruled, .field-label, .han, .scanning, .drops-out) as plain global CSS in app.css, and let components own their own geometry in component <style>. Tailwind emits @utility rules only where its scanner sees the name used, and it has silently dropped this world's classes twice — once because an unanchored lib/ rule in .gitignore hid site/src/lib from source detection, so every mark rendered 0×0 and review looked fine.
Do keep check-css.mjs in the build (pnpm build runs it after vite build) and add any new world class to its REQUIRED list. A design that vanishes without an error is the failure this guards against.

Do implement a view like scanner view as a document state — a class on <html> that re-points the drop-out custom properties to transparent — so every layer, including anything portalled out of the tree, changes together.

Do mark every pre-printed element with .drops-out so it disappears under the lamp, and check a new screen by turning scanner view on: what remains must be exactly what a grader is allowed to depend on.
Do put load-bearing numbers in the mono face with tabular figures.
Do let untrusted bundle content wrap (.han) and let unshrinkable content scroll in its own box.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion; the global reduction to 0.01ms is already in place and no component may opt out.
donts: Don't introduce a radius anywhere, or accept DaisyUI's defaults for radius, depth, or noise — the omr theme zeroes all three on purpose.
Don't add a second shadow, a hover lift, or a zero-offset glow. One elevation exists and it belongs to .sheet.
Don't spend cinnabar on emphasis, decoration, active states, or navigation. If it is not a commit, a seal, or a refusal, it is graphite.
Don't set text in a fill-tier ink (dropout, cinnabar) where it has to be read; the -ink tier exists because those two fail contrast on stock.
Don't implement scanner view — or any state change — as a CSS filter, mix-blend-mode, or opacity fade over the whole page.
Don't put content directly on the scanner bed. The bed carries the footer's issuing block and nothing else; words are read on stock.
Don't use uppercase letterspaced type as a kicker or eyebrow above a headline. It is a field caption and only a field caption.
Don't reach for exam-paper pastiche — torn edges, staples, paper texture, handwriting faces, skewed photographic scans. The world is a printed card, not a prop.
Don't animate anything but the mark's fill. Everything else is a color or border transition of 160–220ms.
